HAVING addressed these bitter words to Ravana, Maricha, full 
of apprehension, said :-" Let us go, but know that when I 
come before that warrior furuished with arrows, sword and 
bow, which he will wield to my destruction, my life is forfeit ! 
Nay, he who opposes Rama will not return alive ! For thee 
he will prove the Rod of Death and thou shalt fall beneath his 
blows. 
In what way can I further thine evil design ? Yet 
I will go. May prosperity attend thee, 0 Ranger of the Night! " 
Highly gratified by these words, Ravana, embracing him 
warmly, addressed him in honeyed accents, sayiog :-
" This magnanimity is worthy of thee; now that thou art 
williog to accede to my request I know thee truly to be Maricha; 
heretofore another demon addressed me. Do thou with me 
ascend my winged chariot, encrusted with gems, to which

" Be it so", answered Tataka's son, whereupon Ravana

stood. Descending from the golden car, the Lord of the 
Titans, accompanied by Maricha, beheld Rama's retreat and 
taking that demon by the hand, Ravana said to him :-
" Here is Rama's hermitage shaded by palm trees ; now 
accomplish the purpose for which we have come hither." 
Hearing Ravana's words, Maricha in an instant transformed 
himself into a deer and began to pace to and fro before Rama's 
hermitage. 
Assuming a marvellous form, wonderful to behold, the 
points of his horns studded with gems, his skin dappled, his 
mouth like a red lotus, his ears azure-tinted, his neck out-
stretched, his belly of a sapphire hue, his llanks the colour of 
the Madhuka llower, shining like the filaments of the Kanja

proportioned, his haunches gleaming with all the colours of 
the rainbow, that demon in an instant had become a ravishing 
gazelle of iridescent hue, studded with every kind of gem, of 
exceeding beauty. The whole forest and Rama's enchanting 
retreat were filled with the radiance of that form, wonderful 
to behold, that had been assumed by the titan.

brief.summary_1line: Maricha reluctantly aids Ravana, transforms into a dazzling golden deer, and wanders near Rama’s hermitage to lure Sita.

image_candidates.scene_text: Maricha transforms into a radiant jewel-studded deer with emerald hooves and rainbow-colored haunches before Rama’s forest hermitage.
Ravana and Maricha descend from a golden flying chariot in the forest of Dandaka, gazing toward Rama’s palm-shaded hermitage.
The glittering deer grazes among flowers near the hermitage, its silver-spotted skin shimmering as it tries to catch Sita’s attention.

deep.rich_summary: Maricha warns Ravana that his obsession with Sita will bring ruin. Speaking bitterly yet resignedly, he predicts that Rama will destroy Ravana, Lanka, and the race of titans, and that he himself will die the moment he appears before Rama. Despite knowing the plan is fatal, Maricha agrees to help. Ravana embraces him and carries him in a gem‑encrusted flying chariot across forests and kingdoms to Rama’s hermitage in the Dandaka forest. There Ravana orders him to begin the deception. Maricha transforms into a dazzling, supernatural deer—its body glittering with gemlike colors and radiant hues—and wanders near the hermitage to attract Sita’s attention. This moment sets in motion the famous golden-deer illusion that will lure Rama away and enable Sita’s abduction, a pivotal turning point in the epic.

highlight_spans.why: Maricha condemns Ravana’s tyranny and predicts destruction, framing the moral and prophetic tone of the episode.
Maricha’s fatalistic acceptance that he will die before Rama underscores the tragic inevitability of the coming events.
Ravana urges Maricha to carry out the plan at Rama’s hermitage—this command initiates the deception that leads to Sita’s abduction.
The lush description of the magical deer reveals Maricha’s supernatural transformation, one of the most iconic illusions in the Ramayana.
The deer wandering near the hermitage to captivate Sita shows the trap being carefully set.

top_scenes.scene_text: Ravana and Maricha flying through the sky in a gem‑studded celestial chariot pulled by mules with goblin heads, forests and rivers far below them.
Maricha transforming into a radiant jewel‑studded deer whose horns, hooves, and rainbow‑colored body illuminate the forest near Rama’s hermitage.
The enchanted deer wandering through flowers and palm trees before the hermitage while Sita glimpses it between the Karnikara trees.
